clue.text: Face up? Anything but!

parts.note: to face up to something is to confront it bravely; the opposite is to retreat from a position or climb down, and the phrase for that pairs the opposite of face with the opposite of up

explanation.walkthrough: Swap each word of 'Face up' for its opposite: the reverse of face is back, and the reverse of up is down.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down or retreat from a stance is the opposite of facing up to a challenge.

clue.text: Stop nagging about car passenger safety advice

definitions.meaning: a curt order to be quiet
an instruction to fasten the seatbelt

explanation.surface: A driver tells a nagging passenger to be quiet, then offers a safety reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for 'shut up' and also a reminder to fasten a seatbelt.

clue.text: Brandy can turn up under a tooth

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word upward means reading it backwards from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone tips a can of brandy upside down beneath a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' turns CAN into NAC, which sits below COG in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brandy distilled in the Charente region of France.

clue.text: No longer popular-except with the boys!

definitions.text: No longer popular-except with the boys!

parts.words: No longer popular-except with the boys!
parts.note: one sense is out of fashion; the joke reading is a girl who has been out with boys on romantic outings

explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the word means out of fashion, except when it describes going out with boys, where it means having had romantic outings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old-fashioned has had its day; a person who went courting has had romantic engagements.

clue.text: Industrial action court

definitions.meaning: a strike in which workers leave their workplace
to woo, as a sweetheart goes out with someone

explanation.surface: A case about a strike comes before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a strike by workers and an old-fashioned phrase for courting a sweetheart.

clue.text: How well owners can obtain a draught-or draft

definitions.text: How well owners can obtain a draught
definitions.meaning: a draught of water is hauled up from a well in a bucket
to prepare a document in written form

explanation.surface: Ways of getting a drink from a well, or of writing a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is hauled up from a well; a contract or plan is composed in writing the same way.

clue.text: Instance of rank potato blight in Hyde Park

definitions.meaning: a line of putrid diseased potato plants in a field
a sandy riding track in the London park

explanation.surface: A gardener reports a patch of potato disease in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London, and the riding track there has a famous name.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of decayed plants describes blight literally; the bridleway along Hyde Park's south side bears that name.

clue.text: Treated properly but showing signs of wear

definitions.meaning: employed well, put to good purpose
much handled, worn from frequent employment

explanation.surface: Something looked after carefully that nevertheless looks worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means employed to good effect, and also worn from much handling.

clue.text: Sorry for writer with single outdoor accommodation

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tent is shelter for camping outdoors

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for an author who camps alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrite person feels regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: A strong drinker should be able to carry it easily

definitions.text: A strong drinker should be able to carry it easily

parts.words: A strong drinker should be able to carry it easily
parts.note: a strong person can lift something not heavy; a hardened drinker can hold a weak beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'carry' suggests lifting a weight, but a drinker 'carries' drink by holding it well; the beer is light in strength, not weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale low-strength bitter beer is easily handled by a seasoned drinker and, punningly, not heavy to lift.

clue.text: Last in fabricating the Marxist Leninist policy

definitions.text: Last in fabricating the Marxist Leninist policy

indicators.note: fabricating means making up or constructing, so these letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: Someone was the final figure to devise Marxist-Leninist doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricating' rearranges LAST IN; the whole clue then describes the Soviet leader who codified Marxism-Leninism as official doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator coined and imposed Marxism-Leninism as the state ideology.

clue.text: Cut up buns

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone slices buns open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BUNS. 'Cut' is the verb meaning to ignore someone pointedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore or rebuff them deliberately.

clue.text: How the Duke of York marched troops in variable health

definitions.text: How the Duke of York marched troops
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the grand old Duke of York marched his ten thousand men to the top of the hill and back
health that alternates between good and bad

explanation.surface: A general's marching orders, compared to someone's fluctuating health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Grand Old Duke of York' is a British nursery rhyme in which he marches his men to the top of a hill and back again.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's marching describes rising and falling, just as fluctuating health does.

clue.text: What the excitable do when in a corner uptight

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Excitable people cornered get tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run inside 'cornER UPTight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitable people burst out suddenly in anger, as a volcano explodes.

clue.text: Vehemently upbraid a silly billy

definitions.meaning: to attack someone verbally
a fool, as in acting like a billy

explanation.surface: Telling off a foolish person in strong terms.
explanation.walkthrough: A billy is a male goat, and the animal's name is also slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means to set about someone; as one word it is a fool or a billy.

clue.text: Vintage cars sought by archaeologists in a kiln site

definitions.meaning: aged vehicles in poor repair

definitions.text: sought by archaeologists in a kiln site
definitions.meaning: ancient pottery jars dug from the remains of a kiln

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig for antique motors at a pottery kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are both rickety cars and earthenware pots, so ancient ones fit both senses.

clue.text: Goad given to a follower to flourish

indicators.note: the phrase for goad is attached to the letter, which goes first

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
to goad someone is to urge them on

explanation.surface: Someone prods a disciple so that they thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a follower' is not a disciple but B, the letter that follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow and thrive rapidly, as plants put out buds.

clue.text: Taken in by a young dog dealer

definitions.meaning: cheated, swindled
what a puppy seller has literally done to a customer

explanation.surface: A buyer was cheated by a seller of puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means swindled into buying something worthless, and literally describes a puppy sale.

clue.text: A period of austerity for the present

definitions.meaning: a stingy era, a hard season
for now, in the interim

explanation.surface: Austerity measures are in place for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a stingy period; as one word it means the interval for now.

clue.text: Invitation for public to visit 24 hrs after golf contest

indicators.note: the day piece is placed after the golf piece

parts.note: the Open is the British golf championship

explanation.surface: Visitors are welcomed a day after a golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open Championship is the major British golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: An event where an institution welcomes the general public to look around.

clue.text: Measure suggested by the Met Office?

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of three feet
headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is Britain's weather service, but 'the Met' here is the Metropolitan Police, whose headquarters is Scotland Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a unit of three feet, and the short name for Scotland Yard, the Met's headquarters.

clue.text: Part of ship which cuts through waves at knots?

definitions.text: Part of ship which cuts through waves
definitions.meaning: the front of a vessel
decorative ribbons tied in loops

explanation.surface: A vessel's prow slicing through waves at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knots' looks like a ship's speed but means ribbons tied in loops.
explanation.definitionFit: The front of a ship and looped ribbon knots share this word.

clue.text: Brass hat from the heavy artillery

definitions.meaning: a high-ranking officer or important person
a large cannonball or shell

explanation.surface: A senior officer from an artillery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An important person and a large projectile share this phrase.

clue.text: In France 1000 or 500 may thus address an English gentleman

definitions.text: In France 1000 or 500 may thus address an English gentleman

parts.note: mil means a thousand, as in per mil
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A French person greets an English gentleman with a large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue says how the French address an English gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French used this term as a form of address to an English lord or gentleman.

clue.text: Determined to acquire a bell over 20cwt

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the bell piece above the weight

parts.note: Big Ben is the great bell at Westminster
twenty hundredweight make a British ton

explanation.surface: Someone wants a huge bell weighing more than a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the famous bell in London's Westminster clock tower; cwt is hundredweight, 112 pounds in Britain, and 20 of them make a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means resolved to obtain it.

clue.text: Drain constructed for cash in Arab countries

indicators.note: constructed means built up from parts, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A drain is built with money in Arab states.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the currency unit of several Arab states, including Iraq and Jordan.

clue.text: Conservative policy which train passengers should get on to

definitions.meaning: a correct approach on the political right

definitions.text: which train passengers should get on to
definitions.meaning: the correct railway track for one's journey

explanation.surface: A Tory policy compared to boarding a train.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the correct railway track and a policy of the political right.

clue.text: A little adhesive looks shoddy

definitions.meaning: slightly sticky
cheap and tasteless

explanation.surface: Some cheap glue looks badly made.
explanation.definitionFit: It means slightly sticky, and also cheap and tasteless.

clue.text: A Royal couple in the Anglican church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Two members of the royal family attend an Anglican service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal' as a noun means a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's or queen's son is a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Leave the hotel to investigate

definitions.meaning: settle the bill and depart
examine, look into

explanation.surface: A guest leaves the hotel to look into a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to settle up and depart, and also to examine something.

clue.text: Polite request for piano hire

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, meaning soft
to lease is to hire or rent

explanation.surface: Someone asks nicely to rent a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: The word added to make a request courteous.

clue.text: Didn't go out with the tummy corseted

definitions.meaning: remained at home
held in, as a belly is by a girdle

explanation.surface: Someone stays home with a tight corset on.
explanation.definitionFit: It means remained at home, and literally a belly held in place by stays.
